name: TX-33
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+18 partisan lean makes a Democratic hold the overwhelming default
Colin Allred is a strong recruit with roughly $8.1 million raised and high name recognition from his 2024 Senate run
Republican Patrick Gillespie shows no meaningful fundraising or outside support
Prediction markets price Democratic chances near 97%
model.rationale: The seat's D+18 fundamentals dominate despite the open seat left by Jasmine Crockett's Senate run, and Allred's fundraising and profile remove any competitiveness concern. Markets and the absence of any Republican financial footprint both point to an easy Democratic hold.
model.watch: Only a major late-breaking scandal or an unexpectedly strong national Republican wave could narrow what is otherwise a lopsided margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jasmine Crockett (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Democrats are heavy favorites to hold this Dallas-based House seat after Jasmine Crockett left it open to run for Senate. The district's D+18 partisan lean gives any Democratic nominee a large structural advantage, and the party landed a strong replacement in Colin Allred, a former congressman and 2024 Senate nominee who has raised over $8 million for the race.

Republican Patrick Gillespie enters with no reported fundraising and no outside spending on his behalf, leaving him little visible path in a seat that leans heavily Democratic. Prediction markets put Democratic odds near 97%, consistent with the district's fundamentals. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on partisanship, candidate resources, and market pricing, all of which point the same direction: a comfortable Democratic win in an open-seat contest.
